title: Cartier fraction covers and strict-local Weil coefficients
statement: Let $Y$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. A Cartier fraction cover is a presentation by open sets $U_x$ containing each $x\in Y$, with sections $n_x,d_x\in\mathcal O_Y(U_x)$ whose germs are non-zero-divisors at every point of $U_x$. On every overlap require $n_xd_t=u_{xt}n_td_x$ in each stalk for some regular unit $u_{xt}$. This is cover data presenting a Cartier divisor; different presentations are not new divisor objects. A presentation has coefficients $W:Y\to\mathbf Z$ if, for every codimension-one $z\in U_x$ (meaning $\dim\mathcal O_{Y,z}=1$), $\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{Y,z}}(n_x)-\operatorname{ord}_{\mathcal O_{Y,z}}(d_x)=W(z)$, where order is quotient-module length (its finite natural-number value, or zero if infinite) as in [def-trf-affine-weil-divisor-class-group]. It is an effective presentation if $d_x=1$ for every $x$; its support is the set where $n_x/d_x$ is not a regular unit. An algebraic cycle with integral coefficients $E$ on $Y$ is the existing locally finitely supported integer-valued function on its points; a Weil cycle is supported at codimension-one points. Say $aE$ is Cartier when a fraction cover has coefficients $aE$. For $f:V\to Y$, define its etale pullback coefficient at $z$ to be $E(f(z))$ if $\dim\mathcal O_{V,z}=1$, and zero otherwise. For a stalk algebra $\varphi:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to H$ and a height-one prime $q$ of $H$, define its strict-local coefficient as $E$ evaluated at the image of $\varphi^{-1}(q)$ under $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to Y$. Say $aE$ is strictly locally principal if for every $y$, residue separable closure $K$, and strict henselization presentation $H$ [def-sc-ring-strict-henselization], $H$ is a Noetherian normal domain and there is $c\in\operatorname{Frac}(H)^\times$ whose existing normalized height-one orders [def-trf-height-one-fraction-order] equal $a$ times these coefficients. The algebra universe may be any universe containing that of $Y$.
